what_it_does: Compact AR/VR glasses and small cameras need to capture images with both very bright and very dark areas at the same time (HDR—high dynamic range), while keeping power low and pixels tiny. This paper describes a camera sensor with three stacked layers of silicon, where each pixel contains its own analog-to-digital converter (circuitry that turns analog brightness levels into digital numbers) and a tiny RAM. By controlling exposure time independently for each pixel, the sensor captures the full tonal range in a single shot. Built-in signal processors correct for manufacturing defects and can skip transmitting boring pixels to save power, accelerating AI and computer vision tasks that run on the camera.
